text: Is it that being caused by knowledge-materials produced in conjunction with the absence of defects is the same as being caused by knowledge-materials alone, or is it being caused by knowledge-materials not produced in conjunction with the absence of defects? Not the former, because being caused by knowledge-materials produced in conjunction with the absence of defects is refuted by the proponents of extrinsic validity. Nor is it the latter. For once it is established that the materials are produced in conjunction with the absence of defects, the causality of the absence of defects is completely obliterated by the method of agreement and difference established otherwise. If it is argued that an absence cannot be a cause, then it must be asked: is an absence an effect or not? If it is not, then since the destruction of a pot would not occur, the eternity of the pot would follow.
